question: Read the federal Grants Data Standards v3.0 element list and JSON schemas (Grants_SDE JSON zip, 2026-06-17) once grants.gov can be fetched with a verified TLS chain, and confirm that the GSDM v1.3 FABS element names used as the federal column of the schema map (FAIN, AwardeeOrRecipientUEI, FederalActionObligation, AssistanceListingNumber, ActionType, RecordType) are the v3.0 names
conclusion_affected: Federal column of daf-grant-schema-map-2026-11-19.csv; whether a DAF record can reuse GREAT Act element names
rationale: grants.gov failed TLS verification through the session proxy (unable to get local issuer certificate), so robots.txt could not be read and nothing was fetched; the map uses GSDM v1.3 FABS, which the Data Foundation describes as the source of the initial core elements and whose domain-value tab names grants.gov/data-standards as authoritative

question: Publish the minimal open DAF grant record as a JSON Schema with test vectors converted from the Chariot Create Grant and Endaoment async-grant examples; choose the purpose vocabulary after reading Candid PCS licence text first-hand (CC BY 4.0 is only reported) and NTEE as the fallback
conclusion_affected: Whether an open grant record is cheap to adopt (field overlap) and which purpose vocabulary is open enough to mandate
rationale: Six of eight core fields map one-to-one between Chariot and Endaoment; purpose is free text in both and coded only in 360Giving and FABS; Schedule I requires only the recipient EIN and an annual amount per recipient

question: Anonymity enum: collect each top-20 sponsor's published donor-disclosure options (full contact, name only, anonymous, fund name, custom) from grant-request help pages and check whether a three-value enum covers them, since both DAF APIs carry only a boolean
conclusion_affected: Field SM-06 of the draft record; Fidelity's 80/15/5 split cannot be expressed in either API
rationale: Chariot has anonymous (boolean), Endaoment shareMyEmail (boolean) plus an optional recommender name; 360Giving and FABS have no donor field at all

question: PayPal Giving Fund donor account terms first-hand: find a robots-allowed, non-403 copy of the US Donor Account Policy (or PPGF's charity/donor help articles) and confirm whether donors hold balances with later recommendations (ongoing advice) or recommend only at donation
conclusion_affected: Whether PPGF's 380,644 FY2024 accounts belong in an ongoing-privilege DAF count (A1) or only in the processor series
rationale: paypal.com policy pages answered 403 again on 2026-11-19; the repo's reading of the policy rests on search-index text [S]; PPGF's 2024 990 has no account-basis wording

question: Classify the account unit of the other 17 DAFRC FY2024 'Donation Processor' sponsors (e.g. Give Back Foundation 7,686; Philanthropi 5,923; FrontStream 1,952; Dechomai 181) from each filed Schedule D Part I line 1, its Part I or Schedule O notes and the processor's own pages, using the five codes in processor-account-counts (donor accounts, employer/program funds, pooled fund, not filed)
conclusion_affected: Processor account series and the comparable donor-account total (786,822 after removing the five processors)
rationale: The five processors examined use three different units (donor accounts, employer program funds, one pooled fund) and one has no filed count; the other 17 processors hold 15,912 DAFRC FY2024 accounts (as published) and may carry the same mix

question: FY2025 basis changes at processors: track AOGF's FYE 2026 column split (695 DAFs; 751,746 other accounts) and BBGF's 2025 statement that CSRconnect employee donations are no longer DAF contributions into the next DAFRC refresh, and quantify the break in processor DAF contributions and grants between FY2024 and FY2025
conclusion_affected: Year-on-year growth in DAF contributions and grants; processor share of grants
rationale: BBGF's CY2025 990 Schedule O: 'BBGF DETERMINED THAT EMPLOYEE DONATIONS MADE THROUGH CSRCONNECT SHOULD NOT BE TREATED BY BBGF AS CONTRIBUTIONS TO DONOR ADVISED FUNDS', yet column (a) still reports $543.8m of contributions; AOGF moved $935.7m of grants to column (b)
